name: Genostabil
description: Genostabil suppresses epigenetic drift in cosmetic and functional geneware by maintaining a controlled methylation environment around modified gene sequences. Without regular dosing, geneware modifications — decorative pigmentation, structural features, bioluminescent patterns, cosmetic morphological changes — gradually shift away from their designed expression, producing unwanted secondary traits or losing intended features entirely. It is taken daily by anyone with active geneware.
effects: stabilizes geneware expression to designed parameters
side_effects: suppresses the body's natural adaptive epigenetic response
prolonged use can cause difficulty with non-geneware genetic adaptation
mild hormonal interference in high doses
street_price: Φ55 per week (generic); Φ180 per week (Lazarus premium)
cultural_context: Geneware is fashion in 2200, and Genostabil is what keeps that fashion from becoming a horror show. The Tier 3-4 geneware community treats it like skincare — premium formulations are marketed with phrases like 'your design, preserved.' Off the Gray Zone, people who got cheap black-market geneware and can't afford Genostabil develop drift syndrome: scales where smooth skin was designed, colors bleeding into unwanted areas, structural features warping.
story_hooks: A character's geneware is drifting despite taking Genostabil — someone has been substituting their prescription with placebos, and their body is changing in ways they didn't choose
A the Gray Zone geneware artist is creating deliberate drift art — clients who stop taking Genostabil on a schedule to produce controlled, evolving body modifications
Lazarus holds the patent on the only effective stabilizer for a new generation of geneware — and is using that leverage to control what modifications people are allowed to keep
